question: An article is sold at a 15% profit. If it had been sold for ₹90 more, the profit would have been 25%. What is the cost price of the article?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in profit percentage = 25% − 15% = 10%

This 10% difference corresponds to the increase in selling price, which is ₹90.

10% of Cost Price = ₹90

Cost Price (100%) = 90 × (100 ÷ 10) = ₹900

**∴ The correct answer is ₹900.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Profit = 15%

New Profit = 25%

Difference in Selling Price (SP) = ₹90

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

 
• CP (100%) SP1 (115%) SP2 (125%) 
• 
• 
• Diff = 10% (₹90) 
• 
• 
• 15% Profit 
• 
• 
• 25% Profit 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) of the article be ₹x.

⇒ Initial Selling Price (SP₁) = x × (100 + 15) ÷ 100 = 1.15x

⇒ New Selling Price (SP₂) = x × (100 + 25) ÷ 100 = 1.25x

⇒ According to the problem, the difference between the two selling prices is ₹90.

⇒ SP₂ − SP₁ = 90

⇒ 1.25x − 1.15x = 90

⇒ 0.10x = 90

⇒ x = 90 ÷ 0.10 = 900

**∴ The correct answer is ₹900.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) of an item. Selling Price can be computed directly as SP = MP × (1 − Discount% ÷ 100).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given on an article, the single equivalent discount percentage is given by [a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100]%.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dishonest dealer sells goods at Cost Price but uses false weights to cheat, the actual Profit % is calculated as [Error ÷ (True Weight − Error)] × 100%.
